key_insight: Strain steers iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3 toward separation or pair-preserving relay hopping, with biaxial compression producing orientation-dependent behavior.
engineering_relevance: Strain and defect orientation may help guide strategies to manage vacancy migration and structural stability in perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies under isotropic and biaxial strain.
DFT and SevenNet-0 static calculations of vacancy-pair interactions.
evidence_signal: Simulations show nonmonotonic short-time hopping fractions versus strain, while static calculations find repulsive interactions in every examined configuration.
watch_item: Short-time defect dynamics do not establish long-term device stability or photovoltaic performance gains.
paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
